category_title: Medicated student struggling with ADHD diagnosis and agency
minimal_context: Dennis and the school pedagogue are in the hallway at 10:00 AM for him to take his prescribed medication.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Dennis, it is 10 o'clock. It is time to take your medicine.

STUDENT: (Refuses to put the pill in his mouth) When I am home with my father, I do not take my medicine. Then I do not have to behave differently and I can relax.

TUTOR: (Sitting bent over him on the floor) You are at school now, so you need to take it. Please put it in your mouth.

STUDENT: (Lying flat on the floor, tense in his whole body, without making contact) I would like to die.

TUTOR: We don't say things like that. Come on, just take the pill.

STUDENT: ...so I don't have to go to school. I want to cut my hand off because it is just in the way anyhow. (Uses a small metal piece from his booklet to scratch his arm)

options.A: Suggest to the pedagogue that they should not force the medication on the student during this session.
options.B: Ask the student to use a self-evaluation template to rate his behavior, record an area to improve, and receive feedback.
options.C: Provide individual assistance in a separate room to help the student understand the reasons for taking the medication.
options.D: Provide detailed instruction of each specific element involved in the daily medication routine during the session.
